info.title: Invinite API
info.description:
Invinite financial data API. Each operation has a base credit cost: `x-credits` is the base cost; responses add 1 credit per started 1,000 rows beyond the first 1,000; `X-Credits-Charged` reports the final debit and `X-Credits-Remaining` what is left of the plan's included credits after it. A `304 Not Modified` costs nothing. `GET /v1/me/usage` returns your account's usage by day, product family and key (it costs no credits).

**Coverage.** Financial data covers US SEC registrants and their US listings; a symbol that is not a US SEC registrant (or a crypto pair such as `X:BTCUSD`) is not a known company and answers 404. A known company with no data in a family (for example no statements yet) answers 404 with `code: not_covered`; an empty page of a covered company stays 200 with an empty list. `GET /v1/companies` lists every known company.

## Webhooks

Accounts on LITE and above subscribe with `POST /v1/webhooks` to the `event.*` lifecycle events (filtered by company) and, on STANDARD and above, to `news.published` (one delivery per new news item, filtered by the companies it mentions); see `x-webhooks` for each `data` object. What a subscription may hold depends on the plan (a create / update beyond it is refused with the plan's limit; `event.test` needs no subscription — the test route and the disabled notice send it to any subscription):

| Plan | Webhooks | Events | CIKs per webhook | Keywords per webhook |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FREE | 0 | — | — | — |
| LITE | 5 | `.scheduled`, `.rescheduled`, `.started`, `.ended`, `.transcript_ready`, `.assets_ready` | ≤ 10 | — |
| STANDARD | 15 | LITE + `.transcript_provisional`, `.transcript_corrected`, `.documents_updated`, `news.published` | ≤ 25 | — |
| PRO / ENTERPRISE | 50 | STANDARD + `.guidance_flash`, `.keyword_hit` | ≤ 100 | ≤ 20 (on ≤ 10 webhooks) |

Every delivery is a `POST` with `Content-Type: application/json`, `X-Invinite-Event`, `X-Invinite-Delivery` and `X-Invinite-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>` where `v1` = HMAC-SHA256(secret, `<t>.<raw body>`); during a secret rotation the header carries one `v1` per valid secret. Reject a signature older than 5 minutes. Any 2xx within 10 s acknowledges; redirects are not followed. A failed delivery is retried after 1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h, 6 h, 12 h, 24 h (8 attempts in all, the same delivery id each time). A subscription is disabled after 8 consecutive dead-lettered deliveries (a final `event.test` with `notice: subscription_disabled` is sent). Deliveries are at-least-once and unordered: dedupe on the delivery id, order by `created_at`.

## Licensing

| Tier | display | redistribute | rag | train | audio | resell |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FREE | ✓ | – | – | – | – | – |
| LITE | ✓ | – | – | – | – | – |
| STANDARD | ✓ | – | ✓ | – | – | – |
| PRO | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | – | ✓ | – |

Invinite data may be shown and, from PRO, redistributed inside the licensee's own product with attribution ("Source: Invinite" on screen or in the API response that carries it). It may never be resold, relicensed, white-labelled or offered as a data feed as the licensee's own data, at any tier, under any contract.

Policy version: 2026-10-draft. Draft — pending counsel sign-off.

Audio files carry a forensic watermark that identifies the recording. Audio is subject to per-company takedown and may not be re-hosted.

SEC data: Figures and filings originate from SEC EDGAR; the standardisation, mapping and derived metrics are Invinite's.

News: News text is Invinite's own summary of the issuer's or the SEC's publication (the publisher's text and media are never served); the licensee shows the attribution (publisher, source URL and date) next to it; the resale rule applies.

PDF documents: Branded PDFs of transcripts and news items are permanent URLs to one shared file per version. They may be shown, downloaded and forwarded unmodified with the notice page intact; the resale rule applies unchanged. News PDFs carry Invinite's summary of the issuer's or the SEC's publication under the attribution stated on their notice page; a PDF disappears when the item is taken down or its source's reuse is denied.

Every `/v1/*` data operation carries `x-license`, the minimum use right its data ships with; `GET /status/licensing` serves the same matrix per route, rendered at [data.invinite.com/docs/licensing](https://data.invinite.com/docs/licensing). `/v1/me` and `/v1/me/usage` serve no licensed data and carry none.

## Status

[`/status`](/status) reports whether each product family works (a status and its uptime over 7, 30 and 90 days); [`/status/licensing`](/status/licensing) serves the licensing matrix per route. The status routes need no API key and are cached for 5 minutes. The public status page is [status.data.invinite.com](https://status.data.invinite.com): a snapshot of `/status` every 15 minutes plus an external reachability probe of the API.

Uptime is the share of requests answered without a server error, measured by the API per product family; a window with too little traffic to judge shows no figure. Status reflects the last 24 hours.

Product families: Company, Financials, SEC Filings, Insider Trades, Institutional Ownership, IPOs, Market, Metadata, Earnings Calls, News, WebSocket, Account.

text.description: The segment (live) or turn (final), at most 500 chars

context_before.description: The previous final / turn of the call (≤ 300 chars); a final is often half a sentence

speaker_name.description: From the live speaker-name snapshot (null while unnamed) or the final transcript

speaker_role.description: executive | ir_host | analyst | operator; null while unnamed

layer.description: live = a live final; final = the final transcript at transcript_ready (once per subscription)

latency_ms.description: live only: relay time inside the API process minus the segment's own end time, so it includes the transcript's release hold of about 8 s (excludes the client's network); null when the call's clock is unknown

WebSocketGuidanceFlashEvent.description: A forward-looking guidance number extracted from the live transcript seconds after it was spoken (one frame per metric / period; a restatement repeats it with a higher revision). Sent to every subscription of the call and to all_live subscriptions whose events include guidance_flash. Provisional: the structured guidance of GET /v1/guidance replaces it after the call

seq.description: The final that triggered the extraction

revision.description: 1 for the first flash of a metric / period; higher when the numbers were restated

low.description: Lower bound of the range (absolute units)

point.description: A point value when no range was given

source_sentence.description: The verbatim sentence the numbers come from

start_ms.description: Milliseconds of the sentence from call_t0

WebSocketPriceTickEvent.description: One second of the call's stock price while the call is live (≤ 1 per second, only seconds with a trade — hold the last value and draw a missing second as a gap; pre-market and after-hours bars are sparse). Sent only to per-call subscriptions with prices: true. Temporal coincidence, not attribution of cause. The minute rows of GET /v1/events/{event_id}/price-attribution are the backlog for a late join

at.description: Start of the one-second bar (ISO 8601 UTC)

call_ms.description: The bar start on the transcript clock (the start_ms of transcript_segment frames); null before the call's clock is known — then chart it on wall time (at)

price.description: Last price of the second, shown while the call is live

cumulative_volume.description: Shares traded so far today; null when unknown

reference_price.description: The call's reference: the last trade before the call start (for a late join, the previous close)

return_bps.description: Return since reference_price, basis points; null without a reference

day_return_bps.description: Return since prev_close, basis points; null without it

source.description: stream = the real-time per-second bar; snapshot = the polled last trade while the stream is down (open = high = low = price)

WebSocketWarningEvent.description: A subscription is degraded but keeps running: global_scope_degraded = a new live call was not attached because this server already follows its cap of live calls (sent once per subscription while the cap holds)

WebSocketTranscriptSegmentEvent.description: One live transcript segment. seq is strictly increasing per call but not contiguous; a partial carries the seq its final will get. Finals and partials are released about 8 s after recognition, a quality hold (https://data.invinite.com/docs/live-sync)

start_ms.description: Milliseconds from call_t0 (GET /v1/events/{event_id}/live-audio), the audio's clock

WebSocketSpeakerNamesEvent.description: Provisional live speaker names (the newest snapshot; the final transcript's naming replaces them). A final's name = the assignment of its speaker_label whose seq range covers its seq

WebSocketCallLifecycleEvent.description: A phase of the call: call_started, call_ended, transcript_provisional, transcript_ready or rescheduled. transcript_ready and rescheduled end the subscription (an unsubscribed frame follows; after rescheduled, subscribe again with the same event_id)

live_transcript_available.description: call_ended only: the provisional live transcript is available (null = unknown)

WebSocketGapEvent.description: No final between after_seq and next_seq arrived within the reorder wait (a capture relaunch skips 1,000+ numbers with nothing lost, or finals were never published). A late final may still follow: order by seq

WebSocketUnsubscribedEvent.description: A subscription ended: on request, after transcript_ready / rescheduled, 2 h after call_ended without transcript_ready, when the call will produce nothing more (capture failed, no call, published), or 12 h after the scheduled start

reason.description: requested | transcript_ready | rescheduled | no_transcript (2 h after call_ended) | call_not_live (capture failed, no call, or published) | max_duration (12 h after the scheduled start)

StreamSubscribeEarningsCall.description: Client frame: subscribe to the live transcript of one earnings call, by event_id or by cik (the call that is live or starts within ±2 h), or with scope: all_live (no event_id / cik) to every call being captured live — keyword hits only, never segments, one subscription slot. Requires the PRO plan.

event_id.description: Event id from the earnings-calls REST routes

scope.description: all_live = every live call (keywords required, error keywords_required without); then no event_id / cik

since_seq.description: Last final seq the client holds; finals after it are replayed before live delivery (-1 = from the first final)

partials.description: Also receive partial (not yet final) segments

prices.description: Also receive price_tick frames of the call's stock (≤ 1 per second while the call is live). Per-call only: with scope: all_live the subscribe is refused (bad_message)

keywords.description: Keyword alerts: a keyword_hit frame for every FINAL segment that contains one (whole words, case-insensitive, multi-word allowed). Held for this subscription only

keyword_match.description: exact = whole-word match of your spelling (buyback never matches buybacks); stem = also s / es / ed / ing / 's per word (tariff matches tariffs)

speaker_roles.description: Only hits spoken by one of these roles (from the provisional live speaker names; a hit whose speaker is still unnamed passes)

min_rank.description: all_live only: calls of companies ranked ≤ min_rank by market cap

events.description: all_live only: what reaches the subscription (default keyword_hit; add guidance_flash to receive the flashes of every live call)

StreamErrorEvent.description: A client frame was refused (unavailable = an unexpected server failure, retry shortly); the socket stays open

channel.description: news for a refusal of a news frame (channel_unavailable = live news is switched off; read GET /v1/news)

StreamSubscribeNews.description: Client frame: follow new news items. One news subscription per connection; a second subscribe replaces the filters. No filter = every item. tickers and ciks together = either; every other filter narrows

sources.description: edgar (SEC filings) and / or ir (company newsrooms)
